text:
rachel: quick QA on scorecard inline help + keyboard shortcut for quick approvals. dropped a tiny mock in figma: https://www.figma.com/file/scorecard/help-mini
devin: looked — love the mini help pill (question-mark). my worry: it's visually similar to disabled chips. needs distinct affordance.
emma: a11y: ensure help pill has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and is reachable via keyboard (tab). suggest `title`+`aria-describedby` for tooltip content.
leo: shortcut idea: `?` toggles help overlay, `a` triggers approve when focus is within a result. confirm mode: hold `Shift`+`A` for bulk approve to avoid accidental clicks.
rachel: good call on accidental approval. i'll wire `a` for single, `Shift+A` for bulk. also will add visual confirmation modal for bulk with undo toast.
accessibility-bot: accessibility-scan: recommend visible focus ring on help pill, ensure 44x44 touch target, and tooltip content linked via `aria-describedby`. contrast passes.
devin: micro-copy: help pill text should read "Help: Scorecard shortcuts" on open; inside list up-front: "a: Approve, Shift+A: Bulk approve (confirm)".
emma: implementation note: don't remove element from DOM when hiding tooltip; use `aria-hidden` toggles so screen readers preserve relationships.
leo: perf note: lazy-load the help content bundle. it's small but good pattern.
rachel: thanks — i'll update figma + open PR with aria attributes, keyboard mapping doc, and tests for focus + accidental-trigger prevention. tagging @devin @emma for review.
